column1: # rule|intent|action|question

complement.care-connection|present|Name one practical support need in a current task and check whether it has actually been discussed.|What are you assuming others know about the help needed to do this work?

complement.care-connection|crossroads|For each option, identify one support need and whether someone has agreed to help meet it.|Which option has a realistic support arrangement rather than an unspoken expectation?

complement.care-connection|action|Make one specific request for support, or clarify an existing offer, leaving room for a realistic response.|How could this exchange make the work more sustainable for both people?

complement.clarity-effort|present|Choose a task and compare its stated purpose with what your recent effort actually produced.|Where is effort following a clear requirement, and where is it filling a gap in the brief?

complement.clarity-effort|crossroads|Define one observable result that would help compare your options, then check the time or skill needed to test it.|What could a modest test tell you that another round of speculation cannot?

complement.clarity-effort|action|Use one clarified requirement to define a short task, then inspect the result against that requirement.|What did this attempt teach you about the task rather than about your worth?

complement.release-change|present|Identify one task carried forward from an older priority and check what purpose it still serves.|What new work is being added before an old commitment has been resolved?

complement.release-change|crossroads|Compare what each option would require you to stop, reduce, or hand over before starting something else.|Which transition leaves room for the new priority without concealing unfinished responsibilities?

complement.release-change|action|Propose closing or handing over one outdated task, checking essential responsibilities before using that time elsewhere.|What needs a clear ending so the next step does not become another layer of work?

repetition.boundaries|present|Choose one responsibility and write down its owner, expected scope, and any part that remains unclear.|Where has willingness to help become an assumption about what you can take on?

repetition.boundaries|crossroads|Compare the limits attached to each option, including hours, responsibilities, and what can be renegotiated.|Which limit protects something essential, and which needs clarification before you decide?
repetition.boundaries|action|Clarify one task boundary with the relevant person, using the time or responsibility it protects as the reason.|What agreement would make this work easier to sustain?

repetition.care|present|Identify one practical condition the work needs, such as usable tools, information, time, or help, and whether it is available.|Which need is being met by extra personal effort instead of adequate support?
repetition.care|crossroads|Compare the support each option requires, including your own needs and the capacity of those who might help.|Which option makes that support explicit and realistic?

repetition.care|action|Address one missing work resource through a small request, adjustment, or use of support already available.|What would make continuing the work more manageable without demanding more from an exhausted person?

repetition.change|present|Name one changed condition in the work and check whether the current process still assumes the old one.|Which part needs reconsideration because the circumstances have changed?

repetition.change|crossroads|Compare what each option asks you to revise and what would need a handoff or support during the transition.|What can change responsibly without pretending the adjustment has no cost?

repetition.change|action|Check one outdated assumption, then propose a small revision within your control before changing a larger process.|What would confirm the revision fits the current work better?
repetition.clarity|present|Separate one written requirement from an assumption about how success will be judged.|What criterion is actually being used, and has it been made explicit?

repetition.clarity|crossroads|Compare the options using one stated criterion and mark where the supporting evidence differs or is missing.|Would you accept the same evidence for the option you currently favor and the one you doubt?
repetition.clarity|action|Verify one consequential work requirement against a brief, example, or the person responsible before proceeding.|What changes once this requirement is clear enough to use?
repetition.connection|present|Trace one handoff in your work and notice what information or help moves in each direction.|Where does a shared task depend on an exchange that has not happened?

repetition.connection|crossroads|Compare who would need to collaborate under each option and whether expectations have been discussed.|Which option depends on support that is available rather than merely hoped for?
repetition.connection|action|Ask one clear question that would unblock a handoff or clarify a shared task.|What response do you need, and what remains outside your control?
repetition.effort|present|Choose a task and examine whether recent effort has produced learning or only more activity.|What feedback would show whether the current approach is useful?
repetition.effort|crossroads|Compare the practice, time, and feedback each option needs before judging it by its appeal.|Which effort serves a purpose you can name and a workload you can sustain?
repetition.effort|action|Work briefly on one defined part of a task, then inspect the result before extending the session.|What did that attempt reveal about the next useful adjustment?

repetition.expansion|present|List the work possibilities currently drawing your attention and identify which has a concrete next step.|Where is interest opening a useful path, and where is it dispersing your attention?

repetition.expansion|crossroads|Compare two possibilities by the learning each offers and the resources needed for a first trial.|Which possibility is worth investigating before committing to a larger change?
repetition.expansion|action|Give one work possibility a brief, reversible trial within your current resources.|What would you need to learn before giving this possibility more time?
repetition.release|present|Review one recurring task or expectation and ask whether its original purpose still applies.|What are you maintaining because of past effort rather than current need?

repetition.release|crossroads|Compare what each option asks you to relinquish and what still needs completion or a responsible handoff.|Which ending would create useful space without hiding an obligation?

repetition.release|action|Propose reducing or retiring one task that no longer serves its purpose, checking dependencies before changing it.|What responsibility must be preserved even as this piece of work ends?

repetition.rest|present|Notice one task affected by depleted attention and which demands are making recovery difficult.|What is the work asking of your capacity that the current plan does not acknowledge?

repetition.rest|crossroads|Compare how each option handles limited energy, time away, and cover for essential responsibilities.|Which plan leaves real room to recover instead of assuming you will simply push through?
repetition.rest|action|Protect a short pause by deferring or renegotiating one nonessential demand where possible.|What would make this pause restorative rather than another obligation?

repetition.solitude|present|Look at time spent working alone and distinguish useful concentration from an unanswered question that needs input.|What has independent reflection clarified, and what remains unresolved?

repetition.solitude|crossroads|Give each option a short private review, then note one conclusion that would need outside feedback.|Which judgment is yours to make, and which depends on information you do not yet have?

repetition.solitude|action|Use a short quiet interval to write the central work question, then decide whether it needs a conversation.|What useful observation can you bring back when the private review ends?
repetition.stability|present|Identify one routine, tool, or working agreement that keeps an ordinary day manageable.|What makes that support dependable, and what maintenance does it need?
repetition.stability|crossroads|Compare the resources and routine upkeep each option would need on an ordinary difficult day.|Which option can be sustained by the support actually available?
repetition.stability|action|Complete one small maintenance task within your responsibility that protects a useful working routine.|What will this maintenance help you or others rely on?

repetition.uncertainty|present|Identify one unknown affecting the work and separate it from an unfavorable outcome you are only imagining.|What is genuinely missing from the picture, rather than already decided?

repetition.uncertainty|crossroads|Mark one unknown for each option and consider which answer could materially change your choice.|What must be checked before commitment, and what uncertainty could you reasonably carry?
repetition.uncertainty|action|Turn one work uncertainty into a question you can check with a relevant source.|What small step becomes possible even if the larger outcome remains open?

tension.care-boundaries|present|Choose one support responsibility and note what it currently costs in time, attention, or materials, including support you need yourself.|Where does the work rely on help that has never been explicitly agreed?

tension.care-boundaries|crossroads|For each option, identify one support need, who could meet it, and a limit that keeps the arrangement workable.|Which option acknowledges the capacity of everyone doing the work, including you?

tension.care-boundaries|action|Clarify the scope of one support commitment so it fits available capacity; request help or propose a smaller contribution where needed.|What limit would make this support more dependable without adding another demand?
tension.change-stability|present|Identify one process that still helps and one assumption that no longer fits the work.|What is dependable because it works, rather than simply because it is familiar?
tension.change-stability|crossroads|For each option, note one support worth preserving and one transition cost that needs a plan.|Which change can you sustain without losing an essential support?
tension.change-stability|action|Propose changing one small part of a process while keeping its essential handoff or deadline covered.|What would show the change is helping before you widen it?

tension.clarity-uncertainty|present|For one current task, separate the requirement you can verify from an assumption about what others expect.|Which missing answer is making this work harder to understand?

tension.clarity-uncertainty|crossroads|Write the same unanswered question beside each work option, then identify who or what could verify the answer before you commit.|Which unknown could change your comparison, and which could remain open for now?

tension.clarity-uncertainty|action|Check one unclear requirement with the person responsible for it, or against the written brief, before spending more time on the task.|What would that answer let you do differently next?

tension.connection-solitude|present|Look at one task that needs both independent thought and another person’s input; note where either part is missing.|What needs private preparation, and what cannot be resolved without feedback?

tension.connection-solitude|crossroads|Compare how each option allows focused work and access to useful feedback.|Where would independence support the work, and where would it hide a missing conversation?

tension.connection-solitude|action|Take a short period to prepare one work question, then bring it to the person whose input is needed.|What can you make clearer privately so the conversation has a useful purpose?
tension.effort-rest|present|Look at one recent work session and note when effort stopped producing useful feedback.|What part of the workload is assuming more attention than you currently have?

tension.effort-rest|crossroads|Compare the time each option requires with the recovery and existing commitments it must leave room for.|Which option remains workable without relying on a sustained burst of extra effort?

tension.effort-rest|action|Choose a short piece of necessary work and a stopping point; pause there before deciding whether more effort would help.|What would tell you to continue, reduce the task, or ask for support?

tension.expansion-boundaries|present|Name one opportunity that interests you and the existing commitment that limits the time you can give it.|What makes this opportunity workable at your current capacity?

tension.expansion-boundaries|crossroads|Compare the options using one concrete limit, such as available hours, alongside one opportunity to learn.|Which trade-off can you explain without assuming extra capacity will appear?

tension.expansion-boundaries|action|Propose a small trial of one work idea with a time limit and a clear point to review it before taking on more.|What observation would justify extending the trial or stopping it?
